title.narrative: Social Support for Resilient Livelihoods Project

description.narrative: The development objectives of Social Support for Resilient Livelihoods Project are to improve resilience among the poor and vulnerable population and to strengthen the national platform for safety nets in Malawi. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Improving Social and Economic Inclusion, focuses on the consolidation of an appropriate package of support for beneficiary households with a mix of program interventions, including social cash transfers, livelihoods support, and enhanced public works, as well as an option for scalable financing in time of crisis. It includes following sub-components: (i) Enhanced Core Programs; and (ii) Financing Scalable Safety Nets. 2) The second component, Strengthening Harmonized Delivery Systems, aims to establish systems to promote harmonization within the social safety net sector and potentially link to other sectors to improve effectiveness of delivering interventions. It includes following sub-components: (i) Social Registry and Information Management; (ii) E-Payments; and (iii) Citizen Engagement. 3) The third component, Capacity Building and Institutional Strengthening Support, aims to provide capacity-building, learning, and operational support for the setting up of the institutional structure necessary for project implementation. It includes following sub-components: (i) Learning and Evaluation; (ii) Institutional Support; and (iii) : Enhancing Accountability and Transparency. 4) The fourth component, Contingent Emergency Response, aims to allow for rapid reallocation of project proceeds in the event of a natural or man-made disaster or crisis that has caused or is likely to imminently cause a major adverse economic and/or social impact.
The objectives of the Project are to improve resilience among the poor and vulnerable population and to strengthen the national platform for safety nets in the Republic of Malawi.

title.narrative: Disaster risk financing mechanism is established for scalable Social Cash Transfers

target.value: Mechanism established and functional in selected districts.

comment.narrative: The design and implementation mechanism to scale up the SCTP and channel funds to vulnerable households in case of extreme weather-related shocks were adopted.  The plan included designing and adoption of the weather trigger mechanisms that will be used to trigger the pay outs and develop a handbook that will operationalize the mechanism and set out the steps through which te scale up would be coordinated at national, district and community levels. The indicator will also track whether the triggers have been met to trigger the payouts. So far, only Karonga out of the six  districts has triggered, and payout has been done.

actual.value: Indicator target achieved. Mechanism established and functional in six districts of Karonga, Nkhotakota, Chiradzulu, Blantyre, Ntcheu and Thyolo.

title.narrative: Disaster risk financing mechanism is established for scalable Social Cash Transfers

target.value: Mechanism established and functional in selected districts.

comment.narrative: The disaster risk financing mechanism remains established and functional as part of the project's scalable safety net architecture. For the 2025/26 season, however, primary rainfall triggers were not met and a secondary evidence review was still ongoing at the time of the mission. This means the mechanism remains in place, but no new large-scale trigger-based expansion had yet been activated for the current season.

actual.value: Mechanism remains established; the 2025/26 season did not trigger drought conditions under the primary rainfall triggers and the secondary evidence review is ongoing.

This new indicator monitors the number of individual direct beneficiaries of CS-EPWP (all members of beneficiary households). The reduction from the previous reporting period reflects the outcome of the retargeting exercise. The review showed that some households were enrolled in both SCTP and CS-EPWP, yet the program requires that a household should belong to only one stream. When correcting the lists, most of those households chose to remain under SCTP because the transfers do not require labor. This reduced the number of households counted as CS-EPWP beneficiaries.

comment.narrative: End target was restructured to to only capture the overall subproject number. Previous reporting counted all individual micro-assets created within each subproject. The revision affected the definition, and does not represent a reduction of the actual work done. Initially, the indicator counted micro-assets. These were too varied to be captured under one numeric indicator because some are measured in numbers, others in length, others in area, etc. Therefore Bank and implementing agency agreed to shift the focus from micro-assets to subprojects, since these can be counted consistently in numbers. The figure of 9,405 from the earlier period already referred to subprojects, not micro-assets.
